show.title: CRE Deal Makers
show.tagline: One commercial real estate company per episode.
show.description: Company profiles of the firms that shape commercial real estate: their history, what they actually do, the deals that defined them, and who they work with. Narrated by Nora and Theo. New episodes on demand.
show.author: Houz Real Estate

episodes.title: Related Companies: From Affordable Housing to Hudson Yards to AI Data Centers
episodes.headline: The Capital Company That Builds Neighborhoods
episodes.summary: How a firm founded in 1972 with a $10,000 loan to finance affordable housing became the developer of Hudson Yards, built a vertically integrated platform with its own fund manager, and closed a $16 billion financing for an AI data center, plus who Related works with and what to know before interviewing there.
episodes.interview_line: Related started as an affordable housing financier and became the developer of Hudson Yards. It's a capital company as much as a builder: it lines up anchor tenants and institutional partners first, which is why it can do 70 Hudson Yards and a $16 billion data center at the same time.

episodes.title: GFP: The Family Landlord Turning Wall Street Offices Into Homes
episodes.headline: The Family Firm Behind America's Biggest Office-to-Residential Conversions
episodes.summary: How the Gural family's 1952 Newmark roots became GFP Real Estate, why it split off GFP Development in 2026, and how it turned obsolete Lower Manhattan towers into SoMA (1,320 units), Wrey (788 units) and 40 Exchange Place, plus the Flatiron condos, 100 Gold Street and the Chrysler Building that got away.
episodes.interview_line: GFP is a seventy-year-old family landlord that turned office distress into a housing pipeline: it buys obsolete Lower Manhattan towers at a fraction of their old value, partners with firms like TPG and Rockwood, and uses the 467-m tax incentive to make conversions like SoMA, the country's largest, pencil.
glance: Jeffrey Gural (Chairman & CEO, GFP RE); Eric Gural (Principal); Brian Steinwurtzel (CEO, GFP Development)
~2,500 homes done or underway, plus ~4,000 at 100 Gold
deals: SoMA — 25 Water St (with Metro Loft, Rockwood)
Bought $251M; $536M construction loan (MSD, Apollo); 1,320 units; first 467-m deal; $835M refi (Apollo, GIC)
Wrey — 222 Broadway (with TPG)
Bought $147.5M vs. $502M in 2014; ~$288M construction financing (BDT & MSD); 788 units
40 Exchange Place
Owned since 2015 ($115M); $191.5M construction loan (Derby Lane); 382 units
Flatiron Building (with Brodsky, Sorgente)
GFP-led group wins auction at ~$161M; ~40 luxury condos; first residents Nov 2026
100 Gold Street (city-owned)
Selected by NYCEDC; ~4,000 homes, ~1,000 permanently affordable
Chrysler Building (lost)
Advanced talks in March; Tishman Speyer and PSP won the ground lease in October
